rationale: C14 is the immediately preceding Flag Day proclamation and supplies the child’s substantive and structural template: recitals about the flag’s 1777 adoption, its association with freedom across race and creed, and the annual custom of observance; followed by directions to display the flag on Government buildings and invitations to citizens to display it at homes and reflect on the responsibilities as well as privileges of citizenship. The child revises and reorders this distinctive package rather than merely sharing proclamation boilerplate. C21 has secondary overlap in its citizenship and race-or-creed themes, while C03 has only the general structure of an annual commemorative proclamation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the American flag...was adopted by the Continental Congress on June 14, 1777
shared_material.parent_excerpt: on June 14, 1777, the Continental Congress adopted the Stars and Stripes as our national emblem
shared_material.explanation: The same historical predicate opens both annual Flag Day proclamations.

shared_material.child_excerpt: this beloved emblem, which flies above all our people of whatever creed or race, signalizes our respect for human rights
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Americans of varied heritage, creed, and race have found refuge from oppression and surcease of fear under the protecting folds of Old Glory
shared_material.explanation: Both use the distinctive race-and-creed formulation to connect the flag with freedom and protection.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the people of the Nation honor our colors by displaying them at their homes or other suitable places
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I call upon the people of the Nation to observe that day as Flag Day by suitable ceremonies and by the display of the flag at their homes and other appropriate places
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts the prior invitation to nationwide private display at homes and other suitable places.

shared_material.child_excerpt: giving thanks for their privileges as citizens under this flag as well as by engaging in earnest contemplation of the obligations inherent in citizenship
shared_material.parent_excerpt: urge all citizens to reflect upon the responsibilities which this banner enjoins as well as the privileges it carries
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves the distinctive paired contrast between citizenship’s privileges and responsibilities or obligations.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I also direct the appropriate officials of the Government to display the flag of the United States on all Government buildings on Flag Day.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby direct that the flag of the United States be displayed on all Government buildings on June 14, 1948
shared_material.explanation: The same concrete governmental-display directive is retained with the year updated and its position reordered.
